channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Judge rules Trump DOJ 'unlawfully' fired Maurene Comey
item.description: A judge ruled against President Donald Trump and the DOJ over the firing of Maurene Comey from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.

item.title: DOJ seeking to charge Comey with conspiring to disclose national defense information
item.description: The case relates to disclosures published in the New York Times in 2016.

item.title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
item.description: The German-owned chain's low prices are winning over shoppers — and pushing competitors to respond. (Image credit: Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

item.title: Anthropic files for mammoth IPO as revenues and losses mount
item.description: US artificial intelligence giant Anthropic files public regulatory paperwork as it gets set to launch on the stock market. Also in this edition: France plans a special disaster fund for businesses hit by riots and looting, and Apple's new top-of-the-line folding iPhone screen shows some unwanted lines of its own.

item.title: Azerbaijan: rare protests over hijab ban in schools
item.description: In Azerbaijan, a new government ban on hijab in schools has provoked rare public protests. The ban prohibits clothing deemed "incompatible with the secular principles of general education". While it does not mention Islamic hijab, girls and teachers wearing hijab have been turned away from schools. The measure has sparked tensions in a country where 96% of the population is Muslim.

item.title: Netanyahu's political survival on the line as Israel heads to the polls
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces a fight for political survival in Israel's election on Tuesday (October 27), with voters weighing his leadership after the 2023 Hamas-led attacks, wars in Gaza and with Iran, and Israel's deepening international isolation. FRANCE24's Douglas Herbert gives us his analysis.

item.title: How election officials are working to mitigate growing distrust ahead of midterms
item.description: Election officials from coast to coast are facing a slew of challenges ahead of the high-stakes midterms.

item.title: Israeli elections: voters turnout reaches '16.7%' four hours after polls open
item.description: A deeply divided Israel headed to the polls on Tuesday (October 27) for the first time since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country's rightward drift. FRANCE 24's Noga Tornapolski tells us more.

item.title: Abortion is on the ballot in Missouri again. Here's what to know about Amendment 3
item.description: Just two years after Missouri voters approved an amendment enshrining the right to abortion care in the state constitution, abortion is on the ballot again.

item.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
item.description: Mississippi has the largest proportional Black population in the country. It's one reason the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending and high-profile campaign visits. (Image credit: Stephen Fowler)

item.title: Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
item.description: Democrats hold significant advantages going into Election Day, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. But lagging enthusiasm among key groups is just one indicator that gains may not come easy. (Image credit: Jason Miller)

item.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
item.description: The prediction market has hired a former FBI official to make sure political insiders don't use the platform for profit from confidential election information. (Image credit: Gabby Jones)

item.title: French football star Mbappe dropped by Chinese brands after 'dictator' remark
item.description: At least three Chinese companies are cutting ties with Kylian Mbappe after he appeared to refer to Mao Zedong, the founder of the People's Republic of China, as a dictator.

item.title: Pair charged over RAF Fairford incident - with suspect accused of assisting Iranian intelligence
item.description: Two British men have been charged with national security offences following an incident at RAF Fairford last month.

item.title: 'They should be afraid': Serbia's student-led victory over Vučić sends warning to 'corrupt' leaders
item.description: François Picard welcomes Helena Ivanov, Associate Research Fellow at the Henry Jackson Society, a London-based foreign policy and national security think tank advocating liberal democracy, strong transatlantic alliances, robust Western defence capabilities and the international promotion of democratic institutions. Ivanov describes the election as a historic turning point in Serbian politics. After 14 years of Aleksandar Vučić's political dominance, the reported electoral victory of a student-led movement represents, more than a challenge to an entrenched political establishment.

item.title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or, with Kylian Mbappé second ahead of Lamine Yamal
item.description: Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d’Or, which was awarded in London for the first time. He becomes the fifth Englishman to win the trophy, 25 years after Michael Owen.

item.title: Live: Polls open in first Israeli election since October 7 attack
item.description: A deeply divided Israel headed to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country's rightward drift. Follow our live blog for all the latest updates.

item.title: Poundland close to collapse as new directors head for exit
item.description: The directors recruited to steer Poundland through its emergency sale process less than two weeks ago are on the brink of resigning, heightening the risk that one of Britain's biggest discount retailers will collapse within days, risking thousands of job losses.

item.title: Meghan 'can't wait' to join Junior MasterChef Australia as host
item.description: Meghan Markle has said she "can't wait" to join as a host for the upcoming series of Junior MasterChef Australia.

item.title: French education reform proposals 'vague': Govt created 'most of the problems' it now seeks to solve
item.description: François Picard welcomes Jean-Rémi Girard, President of the SNALC teachers’ union, who places responsibility for France’s educational difficulties not simply on demographic change or fiscal constraints, but on years of political decisions that, he argues, have weakened the public education system. Against a backdrop of student protests, budgetary uncertainty and mounting concerns over educational inequality, Girard contends that the French government faces the formidable task of addressing a crisis largely of its own making.

item.title: Polls open in Israeli election seen as referendum on Netanyahu
item.description: Polls opened Tuesday in Israel’s critical national election viewed as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s policies. Reporting from Jerusalem, FRANCE 24’s Noga Tarnopolsky explains that “the name of the game” after Election Day is whether the country’s fractious opposition, including an Arab-Israeli majority bloc, can come together to form a government.

item.title: How Trump’s ‘little detour’ to Iran became a roadblock in the midterm elections
item.description: When President Donald Trump launched his war on Iran, he said it would last a matter of weeks

item.title: Judge extends court-ordered block on Trump’s renovation plans for public golf course
item.description: A federal judge has agreed to extend an order blocking the Trump administration’s renovation plans for a century-old public golf course in the nation’s capital

item.title: Another major lender profits in billions as higher bank tax expected in budget
item.description: Another of the UK's biggest banks has posted billions in profits in part thanks to higher interest rates.

item.title: Harry Kane becomes first Englishman in 25 years to win Ballon d'Or
item.description: Kane was followed in the voting by Kylian Mbappé. Spain star Alexia Putellas won her third women's Ballon d'Or. Outside, fans packed the streets and climbed light poles near the London Palladium. (Image credit: Kin Cheung)

item.title: Trump and Rubio plan to visit oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude in Texas
item.description: President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio plan to showcase a newly arrived oil tanker filled with Venezuelan crude in Texas on Tuesday

item.title: Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show in Southern California
item.description: The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday night that Jay-Z will be the featured performer for the halftime festivities on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Image credit: Frank Franklin II)

item.title: Brewers rout the Rays 10-1 to move within a win of their first World Series title
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are one victory from their first World Series title after routing the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night thanks to a trio of young players who have shined in October. (Image credit: Ashley Landis)

item.title: Local ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump starts in southern Ukraine
item.description: A localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, as missile attacks resumed in Kyiv. (Image credit: Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine B)

item.title: Trump campaigns in Mississippi, highlighting Republicans' challenges
item.description: President Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington. (Image credit: Jacquelyn Martin)

item.title: Israelis vote in tense election seen as a referendum on Netanyahu
item.description: Israelis are voting Tuesday in the first general elections since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a fight for political survival. The vote follows three years of regional wars, with Netanyahu running neck and neck with centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot.

item.title: Kylian Mbappé loses two major China sponsorship deals over Mao Zedong joke
item.description: French football star Kylian Mbappé was dropped by two major Chinese brands on Tuesday after a video circulated online in which he appeared to joke about former leader Mao Zedong. Energy drink giant Dongpeng and dairy producer Mengniu said they had terminated their partnerships, citing remarks that offended Chinese national sentiment.

item.title: Users reporting problems with Apple's first foldable iPhone
item.description: Owners of Apple's first foldable iPhone have reported problems with the device's screen - just days after the product went on sale.

item.title: WATCH: Record early voting in key states as Trump, Obama appeal to voters on campaign trail
item.description: President Trump is campaigning in traditionally red states as voters worry about rising prices.

item.title: Jay-Z announced as Super Bowl LXI halftime show performer
item.description: Jay-Z is taking the Super Bowl LXI halftime stage. Super Bowl LXI will take place on Sunday, Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

item.title: Nurse treating Ebola patients killed by machete-wielding mob
item.description: A nurse responding to the Ebola outbreak has been killed by a group of young people armed with machetes, officials have said.

item.title: US-EU trade truce at risk over $3.4 billion Airbus loan, Trump official warns
item.description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned on Monday that a $3.4 billion European Investment Bank loan to Airbus could jeopardise a tariff truce between Washington and Brussels. Greer said his office had received no details about the financing, announced in June, and urged the EU to resolve the matter quickly.

item.title: WATCH: Cruise liner collides with two docked cargo ships
item.description: Police in Germany say stormy weather caused the ship to drift toward the dock. No one was hurt.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro vows to lead opposition after Brazil court imposes travel ban
item.description: Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said on Monday that a Supreme Court justice had barred him from leaving the country after he narrowly lost to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro, who refused to concede defeat, denounced the order as intimidation and vowed to challenge the election results.

item.title: Harry Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or drought, Putellas wins third crown
item.description: Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season. Spain’s Alexia Putellas claimed her third women’s award after helping Barcelona win the Champions League, ending teammate Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign.

item.title: Europe's top NATO powers pledge greater defence role, reaffirm US alliance
item.description: Europe's five main NATO members said on Monday they were ready to take greater responsibility for the continent's security while reaffirming the United States as an "indispensable ally". Defence ministers from France, Germany, Italy, Poland and Britain pledged closer co-operation with Washington after talks in Paris on strengthening Europe's defence role.

item.title: Mecca pact nations hold talks with Iran to prevent renewed Middle East war
item.description: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks in Iran on Monday aimed at preventing renewed fighting in the Middle East, with Tehran describing discussions as “very good”. The diplomatic push, attended by Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, followed warnings from Washington, Tehran and Israel of renewed hostilities.

item.title: WATCH: Paris Hilton on navigating life after adult ADHD diagnosis
item.description: ABC News' Dr. Darien Sutton breaks down what you need to know about the disorder, and Paris Hilton shares more on her personal story.

item.title: Former FBI chief charged for third time by Trump administration
item.description: Former FBI chief James Comey has been charged for a third time by President Donald Trump's administration.

item.title: Protests in Europe: Fact-checking viral videos amid claims of 'chaos'
item.description: As young people protest poor school conditions and the rising cost of living across Europe, misleading videos are spreading online. Footage from Poland in 2017, military preparations in Portugal and a protest in Argentina have all been falsely presented as recent demonstrations in Europe, painting a misleading picture of unrest. Vedika Bahl fact-checks three viral videos to uncover what they really show and how old footage is recycled to spread misinformation and attract clicks.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows soaring sales and steep losses
item.description: AI giant Anthropic has publicly filed for an initial public offering (IPO) with US market regulators. The document offered a glimpse into the company's finances but also contained nearly 100 pages related to risks around investing in the firm. The filing revealed that in the first half of 2026, its revenue soared to $16.3 billion while its net loss widened to over $80 billion. Plus: London's iconic Oxford Street, one of Europe's busiest shopping areas, has been partially pedestrianised.

item.title: Serbia’s elections: 'Tracking fraud for sure had an impact on the results'
item.description: On October 25, Serbia's student-led protest movement won a historic victory in parliamentary ⁠elections, defeating outgoing President Aleksandar Vucic's party. Supporters of the student list explained to FRANCE 24 how they mounted a massive mobilisation to fight electoral fraud and monitor the electoral process inside and outside the polling stations.

item.title: The fall of Sudan's El-Fasher, one year on
item.description: In tonight's edition: 15 military officials in Sudan are sanctioned by the UK over the brutality and abuse of civilians during the fall of El-Fasher. Also, ⁠Algeria is set to send in army units ​to ‌Niger ⁠to ‌protect energy ⁠and economic interests there. And days after a foreigner was beaten to death on the streets of Durban, the stalled asylum process has left many migrants in South Africa living in fear.

item.title: Trump offers $1 million for tipoffs leading to vote fraud conviction as midterms approach
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday pledged a $1 million reward for information on voter fraud leading to conviction ahead of the upcoming 2026 US midterms on November 3. The president gave no details of how the reward would be funded or administered. The comments follow his repeated false claims that he won the 2020 presidential election.

item.title: Israel 'genocide' has continued in Gaza after ceasefire, UN report claims
item.description: Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza despite last October's ceasefire, a UN commission claims.

item.title: WATCH: Brad Raffensperger talks Georgia election security
item.description: Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger discusses election security and the political battle in the Peach State as Election Day nears.

item.title: Serbian student movement eyes power after election triumph
item.description: Emotions ran high in Belgrade on Monday after a student-led movement upset the right-wing populist Aleksandar Vucic's party in Serbia's snap election. A celebratory mood gripped the capital, with drivers honking their horns and passers-by holding up three fingers -- the winning list's ballot number and a Serbian greeting. Many wore badges and other symbols of the student movement, while a large group of residents spent the day cleaning up a park between parliament and the presidency after Vucic loyalists, who had camped there for more than a year, fled. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with researchers and political activist Aleksandar Matković.

item.title: Comeback kid: How did Brazil's veteran leader Lula upset Bolsonaro?
item.description: Just two days shy of his 81st birthday, Brazil's Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has emerged as the comeback kid. Coming from behind in the polls after a bitter campaign where he often showed his age, Lula has become the first candidate since Brazil’s return to democracy in the 1980s to win the presidential run-off after trailing in the first round. How did the Workers' Party leader turn a 2.2 million vote deficit against the far right's Flavio Bolsonaro into a 4.4 million vote win? Just three short weeks ago, most races at the federal and state level broke the way of conservatives and the far right.

item.title: UN cites 'ethnic cleansing' concerns around Israel's Palestinian displacement operation in Hebron
item.description: The United Nations on Monday raised "ethnic cleansing" concerns following Israel's operation to displace by force more than 3,000 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron in the West Bank after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near the city on Friday. UN rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement that the "aggressive operation" must end, and that "collective punishment is a grave violation of international law".

item.title: Trump told DOJ to sue to block Alaska Senate results if Republican narrowly loses
item.description: President Trump says he directed the DOJ to preemptively file a lawsuit to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race if the Republican incumbent narrowly loses.

item.title: Vatican issues Pope health update ahead of South America trip
item.description: The Pope is recovering well from cancer surgery and his trip to South America will go ahead as planned next month, the Vatican has said.

item.title: Thousands of observers are to descend on polling places to monitor on Election Day
item.description: Democrats and outside watchdogs are planning a massive presence at the polls on Election Day

item.title: WATCH: Runners take on NYC Marathon with a mission
item.description: ABC News’ Lara Spencer shares the story of “Team Inspire” as they prepare to run 26.2 miles across New York City.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Macron promises 'concrete measures' over protest demands - amid fears of Halloween unrest
item.description: Emmanuel Macron says his government will unveil "concrete measures" in response to the demands of student protesters for more resources in France.

item.title: WATCH: Homeowners go all out with Halloween decorations
item.description: Front yards are being transformed into Halloween spectacles, with the elaborate decorations lifting spirits.

item.title: WATCH: School janitor gets special honor in tearful ceremony
item.description: Marilyn Hampton was a custodian in the Aubrey School District in Denton County, Texas, who made her mark over the course of four decades.

item.title: WATCH: AI company sued over use of Elvis Presley songs
item.description: The owners of Elvis Presley's music have sued AI company Anthropic, accusing the company of training its models on Elvis' music without permission.

item.title: UK sanctions senior Sudanese commanders 'implicated in rape campaign'
item.description: Senior Sudanese commanders allegedly implicated in a campaign of rape during the country's conflict have been sanctioned by the UK government.

item.title: WATCH: Man arrested near film set
item.description: Police officials say a man displaying a knife was taken into custody and charged with menacing and criminal possession of a weapon.

item.title: North Korean howitzer guns spotted close to border with South Korea
item.description: North Korean howitzer guns have been seen close to the border with South Korea - at a time when tensions between the two nations are high.

item.title: Mariupol veteran who flew in classified mission on what every Ukrainian should know
item.description: "Everyone in Ukraine should know how to apply a tourniquet and how to stop someone's bleeding," Anatolii says.

item.title: WATCH: 2 brothers' Make-A-Wish visit to the Minnesota Vikings
item.description: The Yang brothers got to visit the Minnesota Vikings for Aiden's Make-A-Wish after his brother, Ryan, became his lifesaving bone marrow donor while battling leukemia.

item.title: WATCH: Halloween witches’ world record
item.description: A total of 184 people set a world record, decked out in pointed hats and witches’ cloaks, 400 feet up on the Orlando Eye.

item.title: WATCH: 2 rescued from sinking boat off Florida coast
item.description: Dramatic video shows the rescue of two people stranded in the ocean after their boat sunk off the coast of Fort Myers, Florida. Both boaters are doing OK.

item.title: WATCH: Three ‘hobbits’ dive for hours to find lost ring, return it 1,000 miles away
item.description: In a real-life "Lord of the Rings" quest, three friends and self-proclaimed “hobbits” roped themselves to boulders and spent hours diving into a Tuscan river to find a stranger’s lost wedding ring.

item.title: WATCH: Nat Geo’s 'Moment on the Earth' showcases stunning snorkel cam footage
item.description: National Geographic’s Wonderlab Snorkel Cam, created by Explorer Anand Varma, captures striking 360-degree views of ocean creatures, including a barnacle-covered mussel and a sea urchin.
